notable_absence.finding: The word 'deprecated' does not appear anywhere on this page, nor on any of the eight Server 8.0 pages in this batch (grepped for deprecat|no longer|removed in|will be removed|obsolete across all eight). Two 7.2-era version gates were SILENTLY DROPPED at 8.0 rather than marked deprecated (see version_finding), which is the more interesting shape: Couchbase's SQL++ reference pages do not deprecate, they just stop mentioning. That means a deprecatedIn predicate minted from this corpus will have almost no instances, and the vocabulary gap reconciliation actually needs to close is not deprecatedIn but something like versionGateRemovedIn / noLongerVersionGatedAt - a predicate about the *documentation* losing a constraint, which is only derivable by diffing two version trees and is therefore invisible to any single-page extraction.

cross_product_finding: The Capella twin (cloud/n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/createindex.md) states the SAME 8.0 gate but rephrased for a managed fleet: 'In clusters running Couchbase Server 8.0 and later, the CREATE INDEX statement also allows you to create Composite Vector indexes' versus Server's 'In Couchbase Server 8.0 and later, ...'. Two divergences worth recording. (1) The Capella page carries a WITH-clause 'nodes' gate that the Server 8.0 page does NOT: 'In clusters running Couchbase Server versions 7.6.0 and 7.6.1, you cannot use this option to choose which Index Service nodes contain the index. Clusters running Couchbase Server 7.6.2 and later do not have this restriction.' This is a real, defensible asymmetry rather than a docs bug: the Capella docs must serve a fleet spanning several Server versions simultaneously, so historical gates stay relevant, whereas the 8.0 tree can drop anything satisfied by 8.0. Capella is, counter-intuitively, MORE version-explicit than the versioned Server docs. (2) The Capella page omits the ENTERPRISE EDITION / COMMUNITY EDITION badges entirely from the nodes and num_replica descriptions, and drops the 'In Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition, the recommended way ... In Couchbase Server Community Edition, you need to ...' paragraph. Capella has no edition axis, so requiresEdition facts extracted here have no Capella counterpart by construction - this supports the existing docs-issue capella-pages-cite-edition-badges rather than contradicting it. Server's privilege:query-manage-index must NOT be merged with Capella's privilege:capella-basic-access-write / privilege:capella-advanced-access-query-index; different access models.
version_finding: SAME-PAGE 7.2-vs-8.0 COMPARISON (this batch's cleanest version-drift evidence). Both relations that the 7.2 record based on version-gated prose have lost their textual support at 8.0: (a) 7.2 asserted `n1ql:create-index availableSince version:server-7.0` on the quote 'In Couchbase Server 7.0 and later, CREATE INDEX allows you to make multiple concurrent index creation requests.' The 8.0 page has dropped the qualifier: 'CREATE INDEX allows you to make multiple concurrent index creation requests.' The 7.2-derived definition still HOLDS as a historical fact, but it is no longer *evidenced* at 8.0 - a re-extraction from the 8.0 tree alone would silently lose it. (b) 7.2 asserted `requiresMinVersionFor version:server-6.5` on 'In Couchbase Server 6.5 and later, the index type for a secondary index must be Global Secondary Index (GSI).' The 8.0 page says only 'The index type for a secondary index must be Global Secondary Index (GSI). The USING GSI keywords are optional and may be omitted.' Same fact, version gate removed. Note also that 7.2 minted a predicate `requiresMinVersionFor` that is NOT in the promoted list and is a near-duplicate of availableSince applied to a constraint rather than a feature - reconciliation should either promote it with a crisp definition or fold it into availableSince. NEW AT 8.0, absent from 7.2 entirely: the whole Composite Vector index apparatus (VECTOR keyword, dimension/similarity/description/scan_nprobes/train_list WITH options, codebook, index training), the CREATE VECTOR INDEX cross-reference, and the 'Defer Index Builds by Default' section gating a default-value change on 7.6.2. So this page accumulated two new version facts (8.0, 7.6.2) and lost two old ones (7.0, 6.5) between 7.2 and 8.0. ID-DRIFT WARNING for reconciliation: the 7.2 record used bare option ids n1ql:with-num_replica and n1ql:with-nodes (snake_case, statement-unqualified); I have used n1ql:create-index-with-num-replica / n1ql:create-index-with-nodes because the identical option names recur on CREATE PRIMARY INDEX, CREATE VECTOR INDEX and ALTER INDEX with different edition/deployment gates, so the unqualified ids would wrongly merge four distinct edition-gating facts onto one node. AXIS COLLISION WARNING: the registry's index-type:gsi is on the *implementation technology* axis (USING GSI), whereas index-type:composite-vector and index-type:hyperscale-vector are on the *index kind* axis - all vector indexes are also GSI indexes ('The index type for a secondary index must be Global Secondary Index (GSI)' appears verbatim on createvectorindex.md). These are not siblings and must not be modelled as a single enum.
